headers.//: Mirrors the headers() block in next.config.ts. Static export makes Next drop that block silently, so these are re-declared here; without this the app would ship with no nosniff and no frame protection.
The staff board uses vibration for the new-order alert; nothing else is needed, so everything else is denied.

Firebase sends no-store for everything by default, which would re-download every hashed chunk on each visit and defeat the point of the 103 kB budget. These filenames change whenever their contents do, so they can be kept forever.
A stale service worker can pin an old app shell on the counter phone indefinitely.

Firebase's default is max-age=3600 for everything else, pages included. A page and its router data (/admin and /admin.txt) cached from different deploys make Next navigate the tab to the .txt itself. no-cache still lets the browser keep them, but it asks first, and an unchanged file costs a 304.
The same, for pages served by cleanUrls without their .html.

hosting.//: The cafe's first address, toi-cafe.web.app. Every path on it goes to the same path on toe-cafe.web.app, so old links, bookmarks and any QR code printed with the old address keep working. 302, not 301: browsers cache a 301 forever, and this should stay changeable.
